{{nihongo|'''Tadatsugu Taniguchi'''|谷口 維紹|Taniguchi Tadatsugu|born January 1, 1948 in [[Wakayama Prefecture]]}} is a Japanese [[immunologist]] known for his pioneer research on [[Interferons]] and [[Interferon regulatory factors]].

== Contribution ==
Taniguchi's work is mostly focused on [[immunity (medical)|immunity]] and [[oncogenesis]], in particular on the mechanisms of [[signal transduction]] and [[gene expression]]. While working at the Cancer Institute in [[Tokyo]], he conducted breakthrough research on sequencing the [[cDNA]], and identified two cytokine genes, [[interferon]]-beta and [[interleukin]]-2.<ref>{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1016/0378-1119(80)90138-9
| last1 = Taniguchi | first1 = T.
| last2 = Ohno | first2 = S.
| last3 = Fujii-Kuriyama | first3 = Y.
| last4 = Muramatsu | first4 = M.
| title = The nucleotide sequence of human fibroblast interferon cDNA
| journal = Gene
| volume = 10
| issue = 1
| pages = 11–15
| year = 1980
| pmid = 6157601
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1073/pnas.77.9.5230
| last1 = Taniguchi | first1 = T.
| last2 = Guarente | first2 = L.
| last3 = Roberts | first3 = T. M.
| last4 = Kimelman | first4 = D.
| last5 = Douhan | first5 = J.
| last6 = Ptashne | first6 = M.
| title = Expression of the human fibroblast interferon gene in Escherichia coli
| journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
| volume = 77
| issue = 9
| pages = 5230–5233
| year = 1980
| pmid = 6159642
| pmc = 350031
| bibcode = 1980PNAS...77.5230T | doi-access = free }}</ref> These advances helped characterize various cytokines and discover a new family of [[transcription factor]]s, [[interferon regulatory factors]], which play essential roles in the immune system and cancer.<ref name=r1/>

== Biography ==
After graduating in biology from the [[Tokyo University of Education]] in 1971, Taniguchi worked at the Laboratory of Biochemistry, [[University of Naples]], Italy from 1972 to 1974. He then went to the [[University of Zurich]], where in 1978 he received his doctorate in molecular biology under the supervision of [[Charles Weissmann]].<ref name=r1/> The same year he started working at the Cancer Institute, [[Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research]]. Then for two years he was a visiting associate professor at [[New York University]], and in 1984 was appointed as professor of molecular and cell biology at [[Osaka University]]. From 1995 to 2012, he was a professor at the Faculty of Medicine, [[the University of Tokyo]]. Since 2012, he has been a professor at the Institute of Industrial Science, [[the University of Tokyo]]. He is also an [[adjunct professor]] at the [[New York University School of Medicine]].<ref name=r3/>

== Honors and awards ==
* Milstein Award (1988)<ref name=r2/>
* [[Asahi Prize]] (1989)
* [[Robert Koch Prize]] (1991)
* [[Keio Medical Science Prize]] (1997)
* [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] (2000)
* Member, [[National Academy of Sciences]] (US, since 2003)
* Pezcoller-AACR International Award for Cancer Research (2006) 
* [[Tomizo Yoshida|Tomizo Yoshida Award]], [[Japanese Cancer Association]] (2008)
* Honorary Doctor, [[University of Zurich]] (2007)
* [[Person of Cultural Merit]] (2009)<ref>{{cite web |title=各賞受賞一覧 |url=https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/ja/research/systems-data/d01_01.html |website=東京大学 |access-date=3 September 2025 |language=ja}}</ref>
* Honorary citizen, [[Aridagawa, Wakayama]] (since 2010)
* [[Order of Culture]] (2023)<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.jiji.com/jc/article?k=2023102100173&g=soc|title= 塩野七生さんら7人文化勲章 功労者に北大路欣也さんら|access-date= October 21, 2023|work= Jiji Press}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
* Emory Max Cooper Prize in Immunology (2026)

== Editorial activities ==
He is an editor of the journals ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]'', ''[[eLife]]'' and ''[[Immunity (journal)|Immunity]]''.<ref name=r1/><ref name=r3/>
